SMTO-EXE-0127 — SMTO can't type passwords for you

GUID: 83eaddcb-64bd-5b29-86dd-dc4ac7afcd70
Slug: browser-secret-binding-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO reached a password box on a website. To keep your password private, SMTO never types passwords, so you need to sign in yourself. Nothing was typed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you can use the screen of the Gateway computer, ask SMTO to open a visible browser window on that site. A visible window lets you type your password straight into the website without SMTO seeing it.
  2. Sign in yourself in that window, then tell SMTO in the conversation that you have signed in. SMTO can carry on once the site shows you as signed in.
  3. Never type your password into the SMTO chat. Messages in the conversation are saved and may be shown to the AI model, so a password there isn't private.
  4. If the Gateway computer has no screen you can use, ask the person who manages the Gateway about letting SMTO connect to a browser where you are already signed in. Connecting to your own browser must be set up by the Gateway's administrator.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports that the website shows you as signed in and continues the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't share your password, browser cookies or saved logins with SMTO or in the chat.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser refused fill, type_text or press on a password field because no private secret-insertion route exists.

What this means

  • The exact target is a password control and the requested fill, type_text or press operation has no supported private secret-insertion route. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The exact target is a password control and the requested fill, type_text or press operation has no supported private secret-insertion route.

How to diagnose it

  • Confirm that the requested interaction targets a protected password control; keep credentials out of tool text and chat.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend.execute raises secret_binding_unavailable when the target element's metadata marks it as a password control and the operation is fill, type_text or press; no fill_secret tool exists. Have the user sign in directly in a headed managed session (requires a display on the Gateway host) or an operator-configured attached browser, then confirm completion via ask_user. Never request the password in chat.
  • Ask the user to log in directly in a headed managed or explicitly attached browser and confirm completion. Never request a password in chat.

Retry and execution caution

  • Ask the user to log in directly in a headed managed or explicitly attached browser and confirm completion. Never request a password in chat.

How to verify the fix

  • The user completes the required sign-in through the intended headed/attached browser and confirms completion without disclosing the password.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
